newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian Parliament backs 1997 budget draft.
newsitem.headline: Croatian Parliament backs 1997 budget draft.

text.p: The Croatian Parliament on Friday backed a proposed 1997 budget despite strong criticism from opposition members.
The budget is expected to be approved in December and is likely to include amendments from both the opposition and the ruling HDZ party.
The 39.4 billion kuna ($7.22 billion) budget proposal includes an increase of around ten percent from this year's spending, designed to spur economic recovery and boost welfare programmes.
The deficit of some 2.8 billion kuna would be financed by domestic and foreign borrowing, state news agency HINA said.
Opposition MPs, slamming the government's spending as excessive, claimed the proposed budget was still too "bureaucratic" and "centralised".
The government agreed to provide a detailed report on its spendings over the first nine months of 1996.
